properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 9:54AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
FFWJKL

The National Weather Service in Jackson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Bath County in east central Kentucky...
Central Fleming County in east central Kentucky...

* Until 100 PM EDT.

* At 954 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Flemingsburg, Owingsville, Sherburne, Tilton, Pecks Ridge, Pebble,
Craintown, Oakley, Bethel, Odessa, Elizaville, Reynoldsville,
Nepton, Ewing and Flemingsburg Junction.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 7:28AM EDT until October 11 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Burke County in western North Carolina...
Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 728 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of training cells
producing torrential rainfall moving across eastern Burke County
and entering central and eastern Caldwell County from the south.
This rainfall will be capable of producing 1-2 inches in less than
an hour over saturated soils. This rainfall may cause additional,
significant rises on area streams, including Zacks Fork Creek near
Lenoir; Lower Creek from Lenoir to Gamewell to Antioch Rd;
flood-prone urban areas from Cajah's Mountain to Sawmills to
Granite Falls and along US 70 from Morganton to Drexel, Valdese,
and Connelly Springs; the Yadkin River near Patterson; Kings Creek;
and Mulberry Creek near Collettsville, quickly exacerbating ongoing
Minor flooding.  Significant, Moderate flooding, potentially
impacting some structures and causing significant travel
disruptions, may develop quickly over the next 30-90 minutes.  If
you are near a creek or stream, seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.
Expect significant flooding of adjacent low-lying areas,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-access
areas, and campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and
basements is possible with potential flooding of
first-floors in residences and businesses near streams.
Evacuations may be needed.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Hickory, Lenoir, Morganton, Longview, Sawmills, Granite Falls,
Valdese, Gamewell, Hudson and Salem.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:15 PM EDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 6:29AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 100 PM EDT Sunday.

* At 629 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of training cells
producing torrential rainfall entering northwestern Burke and
southeastern Avery counties.  This rainfall will be capable of
producing 1-2 inches in less than an hour over saturated soils.
This rainfall may cause additional, significant rises on area
streams, including the Linville River from Grandfather Mountain to
Linville and Pineola; Wilson Creek near Edgemont; and Warrior Fork
from Jonas Ridge to Table Rock, quickly exacerbating ongoing Minor
flooding.  Significant, Moderate flooding, potentially impacting
some structures and causing significant travel disruptions, may
develop quickly over the next 30-90 minutes.  If you are near a
creek or stream, seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.
Expect significant flooding of adjacent low-lying areas,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-access
areas, and campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and
basements is possible with potential flooding of
first-floors in residences and businesses near streams.
Evacuations may be needed.  An isolated landslide or two
cannot be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience significant flash flooding
include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, Linville Falls, Lake James State Park, Jonas
Ridge and Edgemont.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.
